title: EXP-036 — Single Button Caption Recovery Across Ordinary Designer Save and Close/Reopen
objective: Using the existing operator-authenticated Mongoose environment, create exactly one new User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_SingleButtonLab01. After confirming its initial clean state and empty component baseline, place exactly one native Toolbox Button, assign Name=FX_SingleButton01 for identity, and set its single tested non-identity property Caption to 'Factory Test Button'. Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after the component configuration and verify the Designer returns clean. Close the target Form using its ordinary Form-tab close control, then reopen exactly the same User-scoped Form through a supported Designer Form-selection or recent-forms path. Verify that exactly one Button with the same Name, Type, and Caption is recovered. Record decisive rendered and property-grid evidence. Limit the conclusion to component-definition recovery across this Save and ordinary close/reopen sequence; do not infer Forms-database durability, cache eviction, or server-side serialization.

in_scope: Review EXP-002-R2, EXP-003-R2, EXP-019-R2, EXP-027, EXP-033-R4, EXP-035-R2, and the existing verified Form/component recipes before browser mutation.
Repository-only prerequisite review as the first worker task, followed by browser preflight in a separate task.
Verify the existing Mongoose session is usable, no sign-in or configuration-selection prompt is present, and the intended Web Designer is available in User editing scope.

Use an existing usable Web Designer when present. If absent, permit one ordinary supported Designer launch from the unobstructed Web Client. Require the actual Designer page and User scope to be visible before proceeding.
Confirm FX_SingleButtonLab01 is absent using a supported Select Form workflow with an observable positive control. Do not create the Form if identity or inventory results are ambiguous.
Create exactly one new Form named FX_SingleButtonLab01 using Category Classic, Wizard BuildFromScratch, and the verified basic-Form procedure, with Save Template unchecked.
Verify the created Form's Name, ScopeType=User, ScopeName, clean Designer state, and empty component baseline before adding the Button.
Place exactly one ordinary native Button from the Web Designer Toolbox.
Set Button Name to FX_SingleButton01 as its identity and Caption to exactly Factory Test Button as the sole tested non-identity property.
Capture the selected Button's property grid and rendered Form layout before Save, visibly showing component Type, Name, Caption, and the target Form identity.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after configuring the Button and verify Save returns to a clean state without errors.
Reinspect the saved Button and verify its Name, Type, and Caption before closing.
Close exactly the target Form through its ordinary Designer Form-tab close control, without closing the Designer client.
Reopen the exact same User-scoped Form through an already-supported Designer Form-selection path, without cold URL navigation or an unload operation.
Reinspect the reopened component and verify exactly one matching Button, Name=FX_SingleButton01, Type=Button, and Caption=Factory Test Button.
Capture before-Save, after-Save, after-close, and post-reopen screenshots and accessibility/property-grid observations with concise evidence summaries.
Use planned evidence captures for each milestone. Allow at most one additional fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection for ambiguity recovery across the entire experiment.
Write repository documentation only to experiments/EXP-036-single-button-caption-recovery-across-ordinary-des.md and evidence/EXP-036/.
Perform a final read-only audit of the target's recovered state, lifecycle action counts, and repository confinement.

acceptance_checks.description: Repository-review evidence identifies the relevant verified recipes and predecessor experiments before browser mutation. Browser preflight independently shows a usable Mongoose session, a functioning Designer in User editing scope, and no visible unsaved changes or session-establishment prompts. Capture the scope and inherited state. If prerequisites cannot be established, stop without mutation.

Before creation, supported Select Form evidence establishes zero exact and case-insensitive matches for FX_SingleButtonLab01, with a known-existing positive-control row confirming the filter works. The selected Name filter and visible result state must be recorded. Zero visible matches establish absence from the observed Select Form list only: hidden Forms can be excluded by the Show All Forms in Forms List preference, so do not claim that no version of the Form exists anywhere.

Exactly one classic BuildFromScratch Form FX_SingleButtonLab01 is created in User scope. A rendered Designer capture identifies the Form Name, visibly shows User editing scope and a clean Form. Record ScopeType and ScopeName where the rendered UI exposes them; if it does not, record that limitation explicitly instead of failing the check. A component baseline establishes no pre-existing Button or other placed component in the target.

Before Save, rendered Form and component-property evidence shows exactly one newly placed native Button, with Type=Button, Name=FX_SingleButton01, and Caption=Factory Test Button. No additional component placement or unrelated property change is recorded.

Before the Save, commit the Caption edit by moving focus out of the property field through an ordinary supported action (for example Tab or selecting another property row) and confirm the property grid shows the committed value; a displayed value that is still being edited does not prove commitment. Exactly one ordinary Designer Save occurs after the Button configuration. The Designer returns to a visibly clean state, and a post-Save property-grid observation still shows Type=Button, Name=FX_SingleButton01, and Caption=Factory Test Button. Save action and result are recorded.

Exactly one ordinary Form-tab close removes FX_SingleButtonLab01 from the Designer without an unsaved-change prompt. The Designer remains usable. Evidence identifies the target immediately before closure and shows it absent from the open Form tabs afterward. If an unsaved-changes prompt appears after the clean Save, do not answer it (neither discard nor save): capture it and stop blocked.

Exactly one ordinary supported reopen loads FX_SingleButtonLab01. Captured evidence identifies the same Name and visibly User editing scope as before closure, plus ScopeType and ScopeName where the rendered UI exposes them (recording the limitation if it does not). The reopened Designer is visibly clean, and no Save, Regenerate, or unload action occurs during reopening.

Post-reopen rendered evidence and the selected component property grid show exactly one native Button named FX_SingleButton01 with Type=Button and Caption=Factory Test Button. These values match the captured pre-Save and post-Save values, with no duplicate target Button. Classify the result as observed component-definition recovery across ordinary close/reopen only.

The final action and repository audit records one Form creation, one Button placement, one post-configuration Save, one target Form close, and one target Form reopen. Evidence establishes no additional component, prohibited Mongoose mutation, deliberate reauthentication, preference change, or unload action. Worker-authored repository writes are confined to the EXP-036 record and evidence directory, with automatically generated tool artifacts disclosed separately. Record recovery allowance usage and preserve limitations.

initial_instruction: T1 — REPOSITORY-ONLY PREFLIGHT REVIEW. Do not call any browser tool or interact with Mongoose. Read AGENTS.md, the relevant EXP-002-R2, EXP-003-R2, EXP-019-R2, EXP-027, EXP-033-R4 and EXP-035-R2 records, and the verified basic Form creation and component addition/configuration recipes. Identify the exact supported UI procedure for creating one User-scoped classic Form, placing one Toolbox Button, configuring its Name and Caption, saving, closing, and reopening. Record the reviewed sources, decisive evidence paths, known limitations, and an ordered proposed action sequence in experiments/EXP-036-single-button-caption-recovery-across-ordinary-des.md and evidence/EXP-036/. Confirm that the browser tool-call count for T1 is zero. Do not begin browser preflight or any mutation. Stop after the repository-only review and report its results to the coordinator.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261009-212412-Gcw7. Rationale: EXP-035-R2 established replay-verified Select Form state retention, EXP-033-R2/R4 established native-keyboard filtering, EXP-027 observed Button component recovery, and EXP-002/003 plus their replays established basic Form and component creation procedures. The next useful step is a small, isolated Web Designer construction experiment: create one FX_-prefixed classic Form, add exactly one ordinary Button, configure its Caption, save, and verify recovery after ordinary close/reopen. A new test Form avoids changing prior experimental artifacts and provides an unambiguous empty-component baseline. This advances toward reliable automated Form construction without introducing bindings, events, scripts, variables, or IDOs. | Specialist review (Infor CloudSuite Assistant, GPT-6): lifecycle valid; AC-2 limited to the observed list; ScopeType/ScopeName may not be visible in the Designer property view; property-grid edits must be committed before Save; an unexpected close prompt must not be answered.
